subject.title: Synchronous transcript I/O scales with tool-result payload size and can block the event loop the liveness monitor samples

question: Should OpenClaw redesign the embedded-run SessionManager persistence path now, and should the accepted direction be async queued writes, chunked synchronous writes, or a narrower payload/liveness mitigation first?
rationale: The bug is source-backed, but the fix crosses core transcript correctness, lock/cache publication, and diagnostics recovery behavior; automation should not choose that architecture without owner intent and measurement expectations.

options.title: Design async SessionManager persistence
options.body: Move append/rewrite work to an owner-approved async or queued persistence path while preserving existing transcript ordering and cache publication invariants.

options.title: Measure before redesign
options.body: Keep the issue open but require a current-main Crabbox/live repro with eventLoopDelayMaxMs and recovery logs before selecting the persistence refactor.

options.title: Limit to payload mitigation
options.body: Treat the issue as a large-tool-result bounding problem and avoid changing SessionManager persistence unless measurements show caps are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Design async SessionManager persistence
recommendation.body: Move append/rewrite work to an owner-approved async or queued persistence path while preserving existing transcript ordering and cache publication invariants.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows steipete involved in the SessionManager append/cache work and adjacent embedded-run changes, making this the best available routing owner for the architectural choice.
